newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares continue to drift lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares continue to drift lower in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares again slipped in weak trade on Wednesday amid liquidity shortage and negative sentiment caused by persisting political uneasiness, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed eight points, or 0.56 percent lower at 1,427. Non-stop losses totalled 6.85 percent since the market opened on Thursday following a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Trade volume shrank to 9.95 trillion lira ($73.6 million) from Tuesday's 11.35 trillion ($83.8 million).

"Trade was narrow with low volume as the market remained totally indexed to politics. It may keep waiting for (political) developments for some more time," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Brokers said firm support expected at the index's 1,420 level was tested in the afternoon. They await fresh support at 1,400 if 1,420 is broken in the next few days.
Hefty corporate tax payments due end-April was another factor hindering cash influx to the bourse, they added.

Turkish opposition plans to form a secularist alliance against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan faltered as veteran left-wing leader Bulent Ecevit acknowledged that two other opposition leaders had only loosely agreed to the plan.

Erbakan who challenged his critics on Tuesday to elections has come under heavy fire from secularist centres, led by the powerful army, for his reluctance to implement measures recommended by the army to fight rising Islamist zeal.
